text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert — us-west-2 / v3-inference canary failing health checks. 5xx rate 18% over 5m, probe failures 3/3. Abort criteria met. Auto-action: CANARY_ABORT queued. Thread: /incidents/1958004321

maria: ack, I'm on it. paging in @sanjay and @alex. taking lead for now.

sanjay: looking. preliminary logs show a spike of backend timeouts from the runtime to the KV cache and a bunch of 502/504s. not yet seeing application logic errors.

sanjay: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR runtime: request failed status=502 upstream=kv-cache-1 connect_timeout
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z WARN kv_cache: connection refused (err=ECONNRESET)
2026-03-15T14:03:00Z ERROR api: 504 gateway timeout, uid=abc123
```

alex: I pushed a kernel/batching tweak ~28m ago to `runtime-v3` to improve batching latency. rolling back now. running: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/runtime-v3 --to-revision=2`

deploy-bot: rollback command accepted. rollout id=rollout-1958004321-r1, pods to update=3. monitoring rollout status...

julia: toggling feature flag `enable_new_batching_v3` -> `off` to stop new code path. Command: `curl -s -X POST "https://flags.internal/api/toggle" -d '{"flag":"enable_new_batching_v3","value":false}'` — verified false via admin UI. :white_check_mark:

maria: good. can someone check open fd counts and connection pool metrics on kv-cache hosts? I want to know whether this is a demand surge or a leak.

sanjay: fd count on kv-cache-1 is high, ~62k, threshold 64k close. connection pool exhaustion showing in traces. suspect connection reuse regression after batching change.

ops-bot: runbook step: rotate pool and restart kv-cache instance. `kubectl -n infra delete pod kv-cache-1` (will recreate via statefulset).

alex: restarting kv-cache-1 now. also increasing connection pool size temporarily to mitigate while we stabilize. patch: `CONFIG_MAX_CONN=20000` applied to configmap and reloaded.

deploy-bot: kv-cache-1 restarted, pod ready. rollout status: runtime rollout 1/3 pods updated (in progress).

maria: customer impact summary so far: ~7 distinct customers saw elevated errors (mostly small teams on dedicated capacity) over last 10m. No broad platform-wide outage. error budget hit for some customers but no billing failures.

product-ops: thanks. do we need to page product-sre / account-ops for targeted customer notifications?

maria: hold on notifications until we have final RCA. I'll craft a heads-up: short note + mitigation steps if errors persist >30m.

sanjay: after kv-cache restart and FF toggle, 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 4% in last 2m. health checks are gradually recovering.

julia: runtime rollout paused at 1/3 after we saw the spike. staying paused until metrics stable.

maria: assigning interim severity P1 (targeted customer impact). Will escalate to P0 if errors exceed 20% region-wide or last >30m.

oncall-shadow: taking the 30m watch. if rollout completes cleanly and 1h of stable health, I'll close the thread and post a summary. handing off to @oncall-shadow for monitoring.

alex: note for postmortem: batching change altered connection lifetime behavior. add integration test for conn pool reuse.

maria: action items:
- roll back runtime patch (alex) — in progress
- disable feature flag (julia) — done
- restart kv-cache pod (alex) — done
- monitor for 60m (oncall-shadow)
- draft customer heads-up if errors persist >30m (maria)

product-ops: update: product teams with affected customers notified to standby. will wait on final confirmation before public notice.

maria: summary for next shift: primary trigger likely connection pool regression from batching change. mitigation: FF off + runtime rollback + restart kv-cache. Customer impact limited and dropping. I'll open RCA ticket and link here.

incident-bot: Canary aborted by operator action. Status: mitigation in progress.

maria: handing off fully to @oncall-shadow. I'm shifting to postmortem write-up. ping me if anything spikes. :pray:
